model_annotation: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of entity types in a biomedical named entity recognition (NER) dataset, likely derived from the paper "From Zero to Hero: Harnessing Transformers for Biomedical Named Entity Recognition in Zero- and Few-shot Contexts." The chart is divided into multiple colored segments, each representing a distinct entity type with its corresponding percentage. The largest segment, colored blue, represents "Chemical" entities, accounting for 32% of the total. The second largest, in orange, is "Protein" at 15%. "DNA" is shown in green at 6%, followed by "Chemical Family" (red, 5%), "Disease" (purple, 5%), and "Cell Type" (brown, 5%). Smaller segments include "Drug" (pink, 4%), "Frequency" (gray, 3%), "Cell Line" (yellow, 3%), "Dosage" (cyan, 3%), "Strength" (dark blue, 2%), "Form" (orange, 2%), "Gene Or Gene Product" (green, 2%), "Disease Or Phenotypic Feature" (red, 2%), "Specific Disease" (purple, 2%), "Reason" (brown, 2%), "Route" (pink, 2%), "Chemical Entity" (gray, 1%), "Sequence Variant" (yellow, 1%), "Modifier" (cyan, 1%), "RNA" (blue, 1%), "Disease Class" (orange, 1%), "Organism Taxon" (green, 1%), "Duration" (red, 1%), and "ADE" (purple, 1%). The chart includes a legend on the right side that maps each label to its color, and all segments are labeled with their respective percentages directly on the chart. The segments are arranged in a clockwise order starting from the top-right, with larger segments positioned more prominently.
